title: Reading what a customer actually wants
target: How to tell what a customer in TCG Card Shop Simulator is doing, using the states the game already tracks instead of guessing from where someone happens to be standing.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: At least one shelf and a staffed counter
A play table if you are running games

steps.do: Watch whether a customer is heading for a shelf or for the counter before you move anything.
steps.because: the game tracks taking an item from a shelf and wanting to pay as separate states (ECustomerState)

steps.do: Treat a card shelf differently from an ordinary one.
steps.because: wanting a card is a state of its own, apart from wanting an ordinary item (WantToBuyCard)

steps.do: Keep a play table clear if you have one, because customers arrive intending to use it.
steps.because: the game has states for walking to a play table and playing at one (WantToPlayGame)

steps.do: Leave the bulk donation box reachable if you want cards brought to you.
steps.because: there are states for walking to the bulk donation box and taking from it (WalkToBulkDonationBox)

steps.do: Expect a queue at the counter before you expect a sale, and staff it accordingly.
steps.because: queueing to pay and being ready to pay are separate states (ECustomerState)

commonMistakes: Chasing a customer who is already on their way out.
Assuming every visitor wants an ordinary item rather than a card.
Blocking the bulk donation box with stock.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
